why.title: The idea
why.text: 21.Rb7+!! offers the rook on b7. Taking it gives White the material back and more.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: 21.Rb7+ puts the rook on b7 where it can be taken by the bishop on c6. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the rook
why.text: 21…Bxb7 is met by 22.Bxb7, taking the bishop on b7. Then 23.c6+ gives check, and 24.Bxg5 takes the bishop on g5. Material is level and White is clearly better (+1.71). This is Black's best try.

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 21.Rb4, is clearly weaker (+0.55 against +2.22). Black answers 21…Bg5, pinning the bishop on f4 to the king. That would leave White a little better.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 24.Re1!! leaves the rook on b7 hanging. Taking it leads to mate.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: The rook on b7 is attacked by the bishop on c6, and 24.Re1 doesn't save it. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the rook
why.text: 24…Bxb7 is met by 25.Bb5+, and the bishop on a6 gets away. Then 26.Bxc6# is mate.

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the rook alone and play 24…Rg8. White answers 25.Bd6, threatening Rbxe7+, winning a bishop. Then 26.Rxe7+ gives check, and 27.Rxb7+ gives check. White ends up a pawn ahead: White is winning (+8.01).

why.title: Why not save the rook first?
why.text: Saving it with 24.R7b5, the best way to do that, is clearly weaker (+0.68 against +8.01). Black answers 24…Kd7, threatening …Kxc7, winning a rook. That would leave White a little better.
